subject.title: feat(cua): add experimental read-only diagnostics provider

question: Should Crabbox ship CUA now as a built-in experimental service-control provider limited to doctor, list, and status while delegated lifecycle support remains blocked on upstream identity primitives?
rationale: The narrowed implementation is safer than the original delegated-run proposal, but it still adds a permanent built-in provider and configuration surface; tests cannot establish whether maintainers want to support that interim product contract.

options.title: Ship read-only CUA
options.body: Accept the experimental service-control contract after exact-head live-account proof confirms doctor, list, and status without mutation.

options.title: Wait for safe lifecycle
options.body: Keep CUA out of the built-in provider set until upstream supports safely attributable creation and deletion.

options.title: Keep diagnostics external
options.body: Offer documentation or an external diagnostic tool instead of adding a built-in provider and configuration namespace.

recommendation.title: Ship read-only CUA
recommendation.body: Accept the experimental service-control contract after exact-head live-account proof confirms doctor, list, and status without mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: They performed and documented the current safety redesign and are the strongest available routing signal for the resulting product choice.
